name: CCSD
description: Existing Chinese sentiment benchmarks are dominated by formally written text. Real user-generated content—including product reviews, social media posts, and online conversations—shares many colloquial phenomena with human-robot dialogue, such as dialect expressions, internet slang, emoji, incomplete utterances, and sarcasm. A classifier tuned on clean text has no reason to generalize to this distribution, yet there is no established benchmark for quantifying the gap. CCSD is therefore intended not only for sentiment benchmarking but also for robustness evaluation of conversational language understanding modules deployed in conversational robots. It contains 6,000 Chinese text samples, each perturbed through a subset of ten strategies that span four linguistic levels: lexical (dialect substitution, phonetic respelling), pragmatic (sarcastic suffixes, conflicting-context preambles), syntactic (rhetorical questions, inverted word order), and surface (internet slang, emoji, modal particles, truncation). Five traditional classifiers were evaluated on CCSD. Linear SVM achieved 83.17% accuracy at 0.16ms per sample on commodity CPU hardware. BERT-base achieved 98.54% accuracy with 92ms CPU latency and 13.57ms GPU latency. These efficiency findings directly inform model selection for service robots and edge-deployed conversational agents where GPU access is limited.
